turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have about twenty minutes before a client call. Owen found out about his mark on his phone, in the middle of your class. Nobody called me first, so tell me why.
Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski.
Mrs. Kalinowski, and you're not going to use it to soften anything. You said I'd be called Mrs. Kalinowski, so I'll hear that. Now tell me why Owen saw a zero on his phone before anyone called me.
The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent.
A machine's guess. Who looked at the essay before the zero went in, and did anyone speak to Owen first?
That's very high. The software is quite reliable.
Reliable compared to what? Even the company that sells it says it shouldn't be the only basis for punishing a student. So what else do you have?
So I had to give him a zero.
"Had to" is not a reason. Who decided that, on what basis, and why was it entered before the parent was called?
I hope you understand my position.
I understand your position. I'm asking you to answer mine. Is there any document besides that percentage?
